# `supabase/rls-disabled`: Row Level Security is not enabled on an exposed table

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| supabase | critical         | 9.5                      | [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Tables in schemas exposed by the Supabase Data API (from `[api] schemas` in
`supabase/config.toml`; default `public` and `graphql_public`) that do not have Row Level
Security enabled **after replaying all SQL migrations in order**:

- tables created without `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`;
- tables where RLS was enabled and later disabled;
- tables with policies while RLS is off (the policies do nothing): reported with a
  separate message.

Migrations are read from every `supabase/migrations` directory (or `supabase.migrationsDirs`)
and parsed with the real Postgres parser (libpg-query).

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Tables in schemas exposed by the Supabase Data API (public by default) can be queried by anyone holding your anon key, and that key ships in every browser bundle. Without Row Level Security, any visitor can read, modify and delete every row of this table with a single HTTP request. Policies on a table do nothing while RLS is disabled.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- Table {table} is in an exposed schema and Row Level Security is not enabled after all migrations.
- Table {table} has {count} policy(ies), but Row Level Security is disabled, so none of them is enforced.
- Table {table} has no Row Level Security in the migrations VibeGuard could parse, but a statement touching it could not be analysed. Verify manually.

## How to fix

Enable RLS in a new migration and add policies that scope rows to their owner. If the table must never be reachable from the API, also revoke privileges from anon and authenticated, or move it to a non-exposed schema. Do not "fix" access errors by disabling RLS.

### Vulnerable

```sql
create table public.profiles (
  id uuid primary key references auth.users,
  full_name text,
  stripe_customer_id text
);
-- (no "enable row level security": anyone with the anon key can read and edit all profiles)
```

### Fixed

```sql
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

create policy "Users read their own profile" on public.profiles
  for select to authenticated using ((select auth.uid()) = id);

create policy "Users update their own profile" on public.profiles
  for update to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = id);
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Private tables:** a table whose privileges are revoked from `anon` and `authenticated`
  (`REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, authenticated`) is treated as intentionally server-only and not
  reported.
- **Statements VibeGuard cannot analyse:** if a statement touching the table failed to parse,
  or a `DO` block / function may change it, the finding uses the `unverified` message and
  low confidence, and the report is marked as partial coverage.
- **The dashboard blind spot:** RLS enabled in the Supabase dashboard and never exported to
  migrations is invisible. If the project uses Supabase but has no migrations, VibeGuard
  says so (`no-migrations`) instead of reporting tables. Run `supabase db pull` and commit
  the result.
- **Limitations:** `search_path` is assumed to be `public` for unqualified names;
  PL/pgSQL is not executed.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```sql
-- vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/rls-disabled -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the statement VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/rls-disabled: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
- [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html): Missing Authorization
